source.security_rationale: CVE-2016-8618: on 32-bit size_t, doubling infop->alloc may wrap to zero. realloc(buffer, 0) may free the allocation and return NULL, leaving error cleanup able to free the stale pointer again. The actual upstream fix initializes newptr to NULL, computes newsize, calls realloc only if newsize > the old allocation, and assigns the checked size. This helper is the changed function in the full fix. Upstream advisory: https://curl.se/docs/CVE-2016-8618.html. Donor formatting is tokenized; explicit C lexical mapping is part of this payload and must be independently reviewed, not treated as a previously ratified mapping.

before_lines: newptr = realloc ( infop -> buffer , infop -> alloc * 2 ) ;
after_lines: if ( newsize > infop -> alloc ) newptr = realloc ( infop -> buffer , newsize ) ;

key_difference: Before patch: `char * newptr ;` | `newptr = realloc ( infop -> buffer , infop -> alloc * 2 ) ;` | `infop -> alloc *= 2 ;`. After patch: `char * newptr = NULL ;` | `size_t newsize = infop -> alloc * 2 ;` | `if ( newsize > infop -> alloc ) newptr = realloc ( infop -> buffer , newsize ) ;` | `infop -> alloc = newsize ;`. Security rationale: CVE-2016-8618: on 32-bit size_t, doubling infop->alloc may wrap to zero. realloc(buffer, 0) may free the allocation and return NULL, leaving error cleanup able to free the stale pointer again. The actual upstream fix initializes newptr to NULL, computes newsize, calls realloc only if newsize > the old allocation, and assigns the checked size. This helper is the changed function in the full fix. Upstream advisory: https://curl.se/docs/CVE-2016-8618.html.
